_comment:
The authored proc/global IO table: one entry per proc or always-on global enhancement piece, keyed by the name the planner looks it up under (set-prefixed where a bare IO name is shared by several sets). Nine authored fields — `setName`, `ioName`, `ppm`, `mechanics`, `pvpNotes`, `type`, `levelRange`, `pool`, `unique`. `ppm` is null for a Global and for some Proc120s, and deliberately null on the Rebirth-only pieces (see `_notes`), which keeps them out of the proc-damage calc.

This is a BASE, not a whole section. `emit-contract.cjs` stitches six derived side tables and two authored ones onto it, in a fixed order, to build the contract's `proc-data` section: the three `effects` tables from `pipeline/_shared/` (globals, then damage, then other), then `ppm`, then `activatePeriod`, then `boostsAllowed`, then `proc-residual-effects.json`, and last the additive `proc-variable-controls.json` overlay. Nothing here carries `effects`, `activatePeriod` or `boostsAllowed`: those are derived and arrive from that merge. `scripts/extract-proc-data.py` reads THIS file for its key list and its `mechanics`/`setName`/`ppm` oracle, so a key renamed here drops that entry's derived side tables on the next regen.

KEY ORDER AND FIELD ORDER ARE DATA HERE, so neither is sorted. `emit-contract.cjs` writes the section with `JSON.stringify(value, null, 1)`, so the order below is the order that lands in every fork's shipped contract, and re-sorting it would move bytes with no data change. The order is also authored grouping, which `_groups` records: each entry names the heading that sat above a run of entries in the TypeScript module this came out of, and the first key of that run.

One shared file. PROC_DATABASE is one cross-fork table — every fork's contract carries the same bytes — so a fork that ever authors its own pieces gets `hand-data/<id>/proc-data.json` and the read in `emit-contract.cjs` grows a fallback then.

_groups.heading: ATO passive-global / pet-proc 6th-piece specials
_groups.firstKey: Superior Scrapper's Strike: Critical Hit Bonus
_groups.note: The binary tags these proc:false (the special isn't a self chance-proc), so they were dropped from the slot UI and the totals — see the extractor's HC_PIECE_PATCHES. Values binary-sourced from Set_Bonus.Global_Bonus.* except Scrapper's Strike crit (a special crit mechanic; std +2/+4%, sup +3/+6% confirmed in-game by @Redlynne). Pet-targeted globals are skipped by the player calc (they buff pets), so they display only; Kheldian's Grace is a SELF global that applies.

_groups.note: Triggers Fear on the slept target plus Psionic damage if the foe was woken early by an attack. PPM per wiki; Superior PPM reported by user verification as 2.5 (wiki uncertainty noted — confirm if tested directly in-game).

_groups.firstKey: Superior Critical Strikes: Recharge/Chance for +Critical Hit%

_groups.heading: Rebirth-only special/proc pieces (interim, hand-curated)
_groups.note: Effect descriptions are binary-sourced (followed the Create_Entity / Null / Set_Mode redirects in the Rebirth bins to the real granted/summoned power), but `ppm` is intentionally null: the Rebirth bins don't expose a clean PPM for these and null keeps them out of the proc-damage calc. These restore the proc-effect tooltip (was blank — no PROC_DATABASE entry). To be superseded by binary-sourced proc effects. See [[proc-piece-name-misresolution]].

_groups.heading: Rebirth / Thunderspy-only proc pieces, read from the fork exports
_groups.firstKey: Forced Indoctrination: Chance for Psionic Damage
_groups.note: Read from exported_powers/rebirth and exported_powers/thunderspy (the Homecoming export the generator reads has none of these sets), so each entry's effects are transcribed in proc-residual-effects.json. Unlike the interim group above, `ppm` IS set: each piece's proc effect group states a clean PPM. Damage is scale 0.67 on Melee_TempDamage (L1 10, L50 107.09 for 53 of Rebirth's classes), the same template as Absolute Resolution. Primal Energy is the Rage attrib at 10 per point (scale 10 = +1, the Superior's 20 = +2, matching each piece's help text), gated off PvP maps.

_notes.+Absorb/Chance for +Absorb: Preventive Medicine (Healing set) — Global IO, health-threshold trigger.
_notes.Vigilant Assault: Recharge/Chance for +A: Vigilant Assault (Defender ATO) — PBAoE Absorb proc.
_notes.Superior Overpowering Presence: Recharge: Superior ATO procs run +1 PPM over their non-superior version (cf. Entomb 2 → Superior Entomb 3, Gauntleted Fist 2 → Superior 3). The base "Chance for Energy Font" is 1 PPM, so the Superior piece is 2.
_notes.Liberty's Belt: Resistance/Global Damage: Rebirth-only. Always-on global +7.5% Damage fused onto the set's 6th (Resistance) piece — the LotG +Recharge analogue for damage, Rule-of-5 capped. Effect in proc-residual-effects.json (category 'Damage'). The IO-set piece is "Resistance/Global Damage Bonus" (see extract-rebirth-io-sets-v2.py REBIRTH_PIECE_PATCHES); findProcData resolves it via the set-name fallback. `unique` is empty on purpose: not globally unique — rule-of-5 like LotG.
_notes.Synapse's Agility: Endurance Drain Resis: Rebirth-only. Always-on global fused onto the set's 6th piece: 20% resistance to endurance drain. The bins grant it as an auto power gated on the F piece being slotted (Set_Bonus.Challenge_Set_Bonus.Synapses_Agility, two 0.2×Melee_Ones templates on the Recovery and Endurance attribs), a shape the set-bonus extractor can't reach — hence hand-curated, like Liberty's Belt above. Effect in proc-residual-effects.json. The auto power stacks to 2 across powers (StackExactPower, stack_limit 2); the planner models one copy, like every other always-on global.
